prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t look up live listings from here, but I can tell you who normally does backflow testing and how to find and verify nearby certified testers for Liberty, MO — plus what to ask and expect.

Who typically does backflow testing and repairs
- Licensed plumbers (many service backflow assemblies)
- Irrigation/sprinkler companies
- Fire‑protection contractors (for fire line assemblies)
- Dedicated backflow testing companies

Where to look right away
- City of Liberty (Liberty Utilities / Public Works) — they often maintain a list of approved/registered testers and can tell you any local requirements.
- Clay County or your water provider’s website — some keep lists of certified backflow testers or require registration.
- Online directories: Google Maps, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor — search for “backflow testing Liberty MO,” “backflow tester,” or “backflow repair.”
- National/local plumbing chains (e.g., Roto‑Rooter, Mr. Rooter) and local irrigation companies often advertise backflow testing.

How to verify a tester is legitimate
- Ask for their backflow tester certification and expiration date. (Most testers carry a state or industry certification; the city may require registration.)
- Ask whether they are licensed and insured.
- Request a sample test report (you should get a written report after testing).
- Confirm they file the test results with the water utility if required (many cities require the tester to submit the report).

What to expect (typical)
- Cost: often $75–$150 per assembly for testing; repairs are extra and priced per part/labor.
- Frequency: most assemblies require annual testing.
- Paperwork: you should receive a completed test report and, if needed, the tester will submit results to the utility.

Sample phone/email script
“Hi — I need annual backflow testing/repair at [address]. Are you a certified backflow assembly tester? What is your tester certification number and expiration date? Do you submit test results to the City of Liberty/water provider? What’s your price for testing one assembly, and do you give a written report? Are you licensed and insured? If repairs are needed, how do you estimate and bill for parts and labor?”

If you’d like, I can:
- Draft a message you can send to multiple companies.
- Give exact search queries and recommended sites to check.
- If you want me to look up specific businesses and phone numbers, tell me and I’ll need web access or you can paste a few candidate names for me to evaluate.
